rendered:
The paper does not give a blind-test accuracy for the ternary bacterial mixtures.

The only blind test it reports was on single strains: Blind tests were performed on four strains at unknown concentrations, which delivered 100% classification accuracy (Tables S9-S12).[1] This result belongs to the section on bacterial discrimination at different concentrations, not to the section on mixtures.

For the ternary mixtures, it only describes the classification in qualitative terms. Mixtures were made with a compositional ratio of 1:1:1[2], and the paper says that the multicomponent bacterial mixtures could also be effectively classified[3] based on the LDA score plots in Fig. 4[4] (panels d–f) and the supplementary figures. It gives no accuracy figure or blind-test result for these mixtures.
